questions.question: What political system in South Africa did Nelson Mandela dedicate his life to dismantling?
questions.explanation: Apartheid was the institutionalized system of racial segregation and white minority rule in South Africa that Mandela fought against.

questions.question: In what year was Nelson Mandela awarded the Nobel Peace Prize alongside F.W. de Klerk?
questions.explanation: Nelson Mandela and F.W. de Klerk jointly received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993 for their peaceful termination of the apartheid regime.

questions.question: What is the contextual synonym of the word 'emancipation' as used in Mandela's historic speeches?
questions.explanation: 'Emancipation' means the process of being set free from legal, social, or political restrictions; liberation is its direct synonym.

questions.question: For nearly how many years was Nelson Mandela imprisoned on Robben Island and other facilities?
questions.explanation: Mandela was incarcerated for 27 years (1962 to 1990) before being released to lead South Africa to multiracial democracy.

questions.question: Mandela stated, 'I have cherished the ideal of a democratic and free society.' Here 'cherished' means:
questions.explanation: To 'cherish' an ideal means to protect, care for, and hold it dear in one's mind with deep affection and conviction.

topics.topic_name: Valentina Tereshkova - First Woman in Space

questions.question: Who was the first woman to travel into outer space aboard Vostok 6 in 1963?
questions.explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space when she piloted Vostok 6 on June 16, 1963.

questions.question: What hobby and expertise helped Valentina Tereshkova get selected for the cosmonaut program?
questions.explanation: Her extensive experience in parachuting at a local aero club was a critical factor in her selection, as Vostok cosmonauts ejected before landing.

questions.question: How many times did Valentina Tereshkova orbit the Earth during her solitary mission in Vostok 6?
questions.explanation: Tereshkova spent almost three days in space and completed 48 orbits around the Earth in her historic solo mission.

questions.question: Before joining the space program, in which industry did Valentina Tereshkova work as a young woman?
questions.explanation: Tereshkova came from a working-class family and worked as a textile mill worker while continuing her education by correspondence.

questions.question: What is the antonym of the word 'solitary' as applied to her solo spaceflight?
questions.explanation: 'Solitary' means done alone or without companions. The antonym is 'accompanied' or 'shared'.

topics.topic_name: Kalpana Chawla - Dedication to Aeronautical Dreams

questions.question: Where was astronaut Kalpana Chawla born before emigrating to the United States to study aeronautical engineering?
questions.explanation: Kalpana Chawla was born in Karnal, Haryana, India, where she graduated in aeronautical engineering before pursuing higher studies in the US.

questions.question: Which tragic space shuttle disaster claimed the life of Kalpana Chawla and six fellow astronauts in 2003?
questions.explanation: Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrated during atmospheric re-entry over Texas on February 1, 2003, resulting in the loss of all seven crew members.

questions.question: What academic degree in Aerospace Engineering did Kalpana Chawla earn from the University of Colorado?
questions.explanation: Chawla obtained her Ph.D. in Aerospace Engineering from the University of Colorado in 1988, having previously completed her Master's in Texas.

questions.question: What caused the structural failure of Space Shuttle Columbia during re-entry?

options.label: A
options.text: Damage to the thermal protection tiles on the wing from falling foam insulation during launch

options.label: B
options.text: Engine running out of rocket fuel

options.label: C
options.text: Collision with an orbiting space satellite

questions.correct_answer_text: Damage to the thermal protection tiles on the wing from falling foam insulation during launch
questions.explanation: A piece of foam insulation broke off from the external tank during launch and struck the left wing, damaging heat-shield tiles.

questions.question: The word 'perseverance' most accurately describes Kalpana Chawla's journey. What does it mean?

options.label: A
options.text: Persistent determination to achieve a goal despite difficulties

options.label: B
options.text: Surrendering at the first sign of trouble

options.label: C
options.text: A sudden burst of unexpected luck

questions.correct_answer_text: Persistent determination to achieve a goal despite difficulties
questions.explanation: 'Perseverance' is steadfast persistence and dedication in doing something despite obstacles, hardship, or delay.

questions.question: Where did Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman deliver his epoch-making 7th March speech in 1971?
questions.explanation: Bangabandhu addressed over a million people at the Racecourse Maidan (now Suhrawardy Udyan) on March 7, 1971.

questions.question: Which international organization registered Bangabandhu's 7th March speech as part of the Memory of the World International Register?
questions.explanation: On October 30, 2017, UNESCO recognized the historic 7th March Speech as a Documentary Heritage under the Memory of the World Register.

questions.question: What famous climactic declaration did Bangabandhu utter at the conclusion of his 7th March speech?

options.label: A
options.text: 'The struggle this time is a struggle for our emancipation; the struggle this time is a struggle for our independence'

options.label: B
options.text: 'Give me blood and I will give you freedom'

questions.correct_answer_text: 'The struggle this time is a struggle for our emancipation; the struggle this time is a struggle for our independence'
questions.explanation: Bangabandhu declared: 'Ebar-er shongram amader muktir shongram, ebar-er shongram shadhinotar shongram' ('The struggle this time is a struggle for our emancipation; the struggle this time is a struggle for our independence').

questions.question: What is the tone of Bangabandhu's speech when he said 'You cannot keep seven crore people subjugated'?
questions.explanation: The tone expresses strong resolve, unwavering courage, and open defiance against military oppression and autocracy.

questions.question: What did Bangabandhu instruct the people to build in every house during his speech?

options.label: A
options.text: Fortresses of resistance ('Build a fortress in every house')

questions.correct_answer_text: Fortresses of resistance ('Build a fortress in every house')
questions.explanation: Bangabandhu exhorted: 'Ghorey ghorey durgo gorey tolo' ('Build a fortress in every house; confront the enemy with whatever you have').

topics.topic_name: The Unbeaten Girls - Women's Football Champions

questions.question: The lesson 'The Unbeaten Girls' highlights which remarkable sporting triumph of Bangladesh?

options.label: A
options.text: Bangladesh Women's Football Team winning the SAFF Women's Championship

options.label: B
options.text: Bangladesh Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup victory

questions.correct_answer_text: Bangladesh Women's Football Team winning the SAFF Women's Championship
questions.explanation: The text celebrates the historic triumph of the Bangladesh national women's football team winning the SAFF championship undefeated.

questions.question: Which rural village in Mymensingh became famous as the nursery of top women football players like Sanjida and Maria?
questions.explanation: Kalsindur, a remote village in Dhobaura upazila of Mymensingh, produced many of the key players who led Bangladesh to international soccer glory.

questions.question: What major socio-economic obstacles did the female footballers overcome to achieve success?

options.label: A
options.text: Poverty, patriarchal taboos, and lack of modern training facilities

questions.correct_answer_text: Poverty, patriarchal taboos, and lack of modern training facilities
questions.explanation: The girls triumphed over deep rural poverty, rigid conservative social prejudice against girls playing outdoor sports, and primitive facilities.

questions.question: What does the title 'The Unbeaten Girls' signify in both literal and metaphorical senses?

options.label: A
options.text: Undefeated in the soccer tournament and undefeated by social adversity

options.label: B
options.text: They never took any physical exams

options.label: C
options.text: They refused to play against foreign teams

options.label: D
options.text: They never trained on grass pitches

questions.correct_answer_text: Undefeated in the soccer tournament and undefeated by social adversity
questions.explanation: The title carries dual significance: they were undefeated champions on the football pitch, and unconquerable in spirit against societal odds.

questions.question: Which word is a synonym for 'resilience' as illustrated by the young female footballers?
questions.explanation: 'Resilience' means the capacity to recover quickly from difficulties; 'fortitude' (courage in adversity) is a direct synonym.

questions.question: What is the synonym of the word 'icon' in the sentence 'Mandela is an icon of peace and reconciliation'?
questions.explanation: An 'icon' in this context refers to a person or thing regarded as a representative symbol worthy of veneration.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'reconciliation'?
questions.explanation: 'Reconciliation' means restoring friendly relations. Its direct antonym is 'estrangement' or 'alienation'.

questions.question: In the text, 'cosmonaut' refers to an astronaut from which country/space program?
questions.explanation: The term 'cosmonaut' specifically designates a traveler of the Soviet/Russian space program, derived from Russian 'kosmonavt'.

questions.question: What does 'unwavering' mean in the phrase 'unwavering dedication to freedom'?
questions.explanation: 'Unwavering' means steady, resolute, firm, and not changing or faltering.

questions.question: What is the noun form of the verb 'subjugate'?
questions.explanation: The nominal form derived from the verb 'subjugate' is 'subjugation' (the action of bringing under domination or control).

questions.question: Complete the sentence grammatically: 'Not only Mandela but also his comrades ______ imprisoned for decades.'
questions.explanation: In 'not only... but also...', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('his comrades', plural), hence 'were'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'Kalpana Chawla set off ______ her final space mission in 2003.'
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'set off on a journey/mission', meaning to embark on an undertaking.

questions.question: 'Despite being born in a poor village, the girls refused to give up.' What part of speech is 'Despite'?
questions.explanation: 'Despite' functions as a preposition followed by a noun phrase or gerund ('being born').

questions.question: Identify the correct passive form of: 'Bangabandhu delivered the historic speech.'

options.label: A
options.text: The historic speech was delivered by Bangabandhu.

options.label: B
options.text: The historic speech is delivered by Bangabandhu.

options.label: C
options.text: The historic speech had delivered by Bangabandhu.

options.label: D
options.text: The historic speech was being delivered by Bangabandhu.

questions.correct_answer_text: The historic speech was delivered by Bangabandhu.
questions.explanation: Simple past active 'delivered' converts into 'was delivered' in passive voice.

questions.question: 'No sooner had Tereshkova returned from space ______ she was awarded the Hero of the Soviet Union.'
questions.explanation: The correlative structure is 'No sooner had... than...'.

questions.question: What figure of speech is present in Bangabandhu's metaphor 'Build a fortress in every house'?
questions.explanation: Comparing every household directly to a military fortress without using 'like' or 'as' is a metaphor.

questions.question: In Mandela's address, the phrase 'rainbow nation' is an example of:

options.label: A
options.text: Metaphor representing racial unity and diversity

questions.correct_answer_text: Metaphor representing racial unity and diversity
questions.explanation: 'Rainbow nation' metaphorically conveys the peaceful coexistence of people of different skin colors and ethnic heritages in South Africa.

questions.question: What is the primary mood evoked by the narrative of Kalpana Chawla's final mission?
questions.explanation: Her heroic pursuit of space exploration inspires readers, while her sudden untimely death evokes deep sorrow (poignancy).

questions.question: The repetition of the word 'struggle' in Bangabandhu's speech serves what rhetorical purpose?

options.label: A
options.text: To emphasize urgency and rally collective national spirit

questions.correct_answer_text: To emphasize urgency and rally collective national spirit
questions.explanation: Rhetorical repetition (anaphora/parallelism) reinforces central themes, creating a powerful emotional crescendo in political oratory.

questions.question: Which quality best epitomizes all the personalities featured in this unit?

options.label: A
options.text: Uncommon courage and steadfast pursuit of freedom and excellence

options.label: B
options.text: Desire for immense personal monetary wealth

questions.correct_answer_text: Uncommon courage and steadfast pursuit of freedom and excellence
questions.explanation: Every figure (Mandela, Tereshkova, Chawla, Bangabandhu, the Unbeaten Girls) demonstrates courage, resilience, and groundbreaking historic achievement.

questions.question: What major historic proclamation did the 7th March speech effectively set in motion?

options.label: A
options.text: The Liberation War of Bangladesh in 1971

questions.correct_answer_text: The Liberation War of Bangladesh in 1971
questions.explanation: The 7th March address mentally and practically prepared the Bengali nation for the armed Liberation War leading to independence in 1971.

questions.question: What is the global legacy of Nelson Mandela's transition of power in South Africa?

options.label: A
options.text: A triumph of peace, democratic reconciliation, and forgiveness over civil bloodshed

options.label: B
options.text: The division of the nation into several warring states

options.label: C
options.text: The total expulsion of minority communities

options.label: D
options.text: The establishment of a military dictatorship

questions.correct_answer_text: A triumph of peace, democratic reconciliation, and forgiveness over civil bloodshed
questions.explanation: Mandela's Truth and Reconciliation Commission averted civil war and proved that hatred can be overcome by forgiveness and justice.

questions.question: How did Valentina Tereshkova and Kalpana Chawla shatter gender stereotypes worldwide?

options.label: A
options.text: By demonstrating that women can excel at the highest frontiers of science, aviation, and space exploration

options.label: D
options.text: By restricting their studies to domestic arts

questions.correct_answer_text: By demonstrating that women can excel at the highest frontiers of science, aviation, and space exploration
questions.explanation: Their historic flights proved women's capability in previously male-dominated aerospace engineering, inspiring millions of young girls.

questions.question: What message does the victory of the Kalsindur football girls send to society?

options.label: A
options.text: Given equal opportunity and support, girls from marginalized backgrounds can conquer the world

options.label: B
options.text: Sports should only be played in metropolitan schools

options.label: D
options.text: Tradition should always restrict women's freedom

questions.correct_answer_text: Given equal opportunity and support, girls from marginalized backgrounds can conquer the world
questions.explanation: The success of the Kalsindur players is a living testament to female empowerment, hard work, and rural potential.

questions.question: Which personality declared in the dock, 'I have fought against white domination, and I have fought against black domination'?
questions.explanation: Mandela delivered this famous defense statement during the Rivonia Trial in 1964 before being sentenced to life imprisonment.

questions.question: Why did Bangabandhu call for a non-cooperation movement and shutdown of offices in March 1971?

options.label: A
options.text: To protest the Pakistani military regime's refusal to hand over power to the elected majority

options.label: C
options.text: Due to a severe economic recession

options.label: D
options.text: To prepare for routine general elections

questions.correct_answer_text: To protest the Pakistani military regime's refusal to hand over power to the elected majority
questions.explanation: General Yahya Khan postponed the National Assembly session to deny the Awami League its democratic right following the 1970 landslide election win.

questions.question: What was the call sign of Valentina Tereshkova during her space flight?
questions.explanation: Tereshkova's radio call sign during her Vostok 6 mission was 'Chaika' (Russian for 'Seagull').

questions.question: What was Kalpana Chawla's advice to young dreamers aiming for ambitious horizons?

options.label: A
options.text: 'The path from dreams to success does exist. May you have the vision to find it, the courage to get on to it, and the perseverance to follow it.'

options.label: B
options.text: 'Do not dream big dreams because failure is inevitable.'

options.label: D
options.text: 'Money is the only metric of achievement.'

questions.correct_answer_text: 'The path from dreams to success does exist. May you have the vision to find it, the courage to get on to it, and the perseverance to follow it.'
questions.explanation: Chawla sent this uplifting message from Columbia to students of her alma mater, Punjab Engineering College.

questions.question: What is the primary stylistic attribute of Bangabandhu's delivery on 7th March?

options.label: A
options.text: Spontaneous, extempore speech delivered without any written script

options.label: B
options.text: Read mechanically from a prepared manuscript

questions.correct_answer_text: Spontaneous, extempore speech delivered without any written script
questions.explanation: Bangabandhu delivered the 19-minute speech completely extempore without reading from notes, speaking straight from his heart to the people.

questions.question: In the sentence 'Their victory ignited a newfound pride across the nation', what does 'ignited' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Ignited' is used figuratively to mean stimulated, aroused, or set into vibrant motion.
